correctness.rationale: Using the + sign Gauss sum for p≡1 mod4, G=I/2+(sqrt(p) S_{chi(2),chi(3)}-J)/(2p), where S off-diagonal is the quadratic character of each gap 1,2,3. Reflection j↔3-j reduces G to two real 2x2 blocks on even/odd modes; the supplied matrices have off-diagonals depending on chi2 and their characteristic quadratic polynomials give all four eigenvalue branches. Quadratic reciprocity determines (chi2,chi3) by p mod24; direct ordering of roots and solving eigenvector equations yield equality subspaces including phi=(1+sqrt5)/2. Vandermonde in four distinct sampling phases gives full column rank when (p-1)/2>=4, i.e. p>=13; p=5 has rank two, nullity two. Exact branches give the stated scaled asymptotic deficits. Independently built Fourier matrices on eight representative primes from all four classes and diagonalized Gram with NumPy; eigenvalues agreed with formulas to well below 2e-13. Classical Gauss sum is a premise, not independently proved by finite testing.
residual_risks: No full matrix-by-matrix symbolic characteristic-polynomial certificate was generated independently; two-by-two block derivation was checked analytically, and numeric tests corroborate.
